title: Illumina DNA Library Preparation
purpose: To convert 1–500 ng of genomic DNA into dual-indexed, sequencing-ready Illumina libraries (insert size about 300–350 bp) using the Illumina DNA Prep workflow.
principle: Bead-bound transposomes (BLT) fragment DNA and add adapters in one tagmentation reaction; above about 100 ng input the beads saturate, so yield self-normalises [1]. After a wash, reduced-cycle PCR adds unique dual indexes, and a bead cleanup removes primers and size-selects before pooling [1][2][3][4].

materials.detail: BLT, TB1, TSB, TWB, EPM, RSB, IPB [1][2]
Qubit dsDNA assay; Bioanalyzer, TapeStation or Fragment Analyzer [2]

steps.text: Equilibrate reagents per the guide: BLT at 2–8 °C (never below 2 °C); TB1, EPM, RSB at −25 to −15 °C; IPB, TSB, TWB at room temperature [2].
Quantify input DNA fluorometrically and dilute to 1–500 ng in up to 30 µL; seal plates for all shaking, cycling and spinning [2].
Vortex BLT well (do not spin it down first). Make a master mix of 11 µL BLT and 11 µL TB1 per sample [2].
Add 20 µL master mix to each 30 µL DNA sample and mix by pipetting 10 times [2].
Run TAG: 55 °C for 15 min, hold 10 °C (50 µL, heated lid 100 °C) [2].
Add 10 µL TSB, mix 10 times and incubate at 37 °C, hold 10 °C [2].
Place on the magnet until clear (about 3 min) and discard the supernatant [2].
Wash the beads twice with 100 µL TWB, adding slowly to avoid foaming; remove the last wash fully [2].
Add PCR master mix (EPM plus water) and unique i7/i5 index adapters to the washed beads and mix [2][4].
Amplify with a reduced-cycle program; cycles depend on input, so use the cycle table in the current guide (not verified here) [2][3][4].
Double-sided bead cleanup (first fraction removes large fragments, second captures the library); wash twice with 80% ethanol; elute in RSB [2][3][4].
Pool: equal volume for 100–500 ng inputs; below 100 ng quantify each library and pool equimolar [1][2][3].
Check the pool on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation: smear near 400–700 bp, no adapter dimer [2][3].
Quantify by Qubit, calculate molarity and dilute to your sequencer's loading concentration. Store at −25 to −15 °C [2].

results: Peak insert about 300–350 bp with a broad distribution of roughly 250–1000 bp [1][2].
Pooled libraries free of adapter dimer, with enough concentration to dilute to the loading concentration.
controls: Include a no-template (water) control through tagmentation and PCR
Quantify input fluorometrically, not by A260 alone
Use unique dual indexes to detect index cross-talk

troubleshooting.cause: Low or degraded input; EDTA or ethanol carry-over
troubleshooting.fix: Re-quantify; clean the DNA; adjust PCR cycles per guide [2]
Repeat bead cleanup; avoid excess cycles [3]

safety: Tagmentation reagents are potentially hazardous: wear eye protection, gloves and a lab coat; treat used reagents as chemical waste; check the SDS [2].
Blood used with the optional lysis workflow is a biohazard [2].
Keep pre- and post-PCR areas physically separate to avoid contamination [3].
For Research Use Only; not for diagnostic procedures [1].
